text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- U.S. military likely to strengthen American forward presence in the Asia-Pacific region rather than reduce its troops deployed there.
- Singapore Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong says at opening of annual ministerial dialogue time has come for European Union and ASEAN to take long-standing relationship to new level.
- Cellular phones carry same risk as drunk driving according to study in New England Journal of Medicine.
- Khoo Teck Puat puts Boulevard Hotel on market again with asking price of Singapore $550-600 million.
- Singapore Telecom and new operator, M1, may introduce pre-paid card service for GSM mobile phone users to replace current system of mailing bills.
- Stock Exchange of Singapore volume hits three-year high on buying wave.
- Hang Seng slides while Jakarta bourse touches record high.
- Hotel Properties Ltd negotiating to buy over Forum The Shopping Mall on Orchard Road, which has potential to be redeveloped into bigger commerical complex.
- Acma Ltd agrees to sell its 21 percent stake in Malaysian unit Lityan Holdings to gain about Singapore $61 million or 37 cents a share.
- Hong Kong-listed Far East Holdings International gives Kuala Lumpur-listed Kemayan Corp option to buy office units of building for Singapore $57 million.
- Major property stocks up on confidence in economy.
- Listed Resources Development Corp awards building contract to Sembawang Construction for U.S.$21.65 million.
- Cycle & Carriage Ltd enters into agreement with two Australian companies to set up motor-finance outfit in Australia.
